problem:
The center of the hyperbola $9{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}+54y+10x=-20$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}+54y+10x & =-20 \\ 9{y}^{2}+54y-{x}^{2}+10x & =-20 \\ 9[{y}^{2}+6y]-[{x}^{2}-10x] & =-20 \\ 9[(y+3)^{2}-9]-[(x-5)^{2}-25] & =-20 \\ 9(y+3)^{2}-81-(x-5)^{2}+25 & =-20 \\ 9(y+3)^{2}-(x-5)^{2} & =-20+81-25 \\ 9(y+3)^{2}-(x-5)^{2} & =36 \\ \frac{(y+3)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x-5)^{2}}{36} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-(-3))^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x-5)^{2}}{36} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,5,-3\,).$
